Below are some discreet, guest-friendly spots in an apartment’s shared areas where you can mount security cameras to maximize safety while respecting privacy. Before installing, always:

 •  Check local/state laws on video surveillance

1. Main Entrance / Foyer  
   •  Mount height: 8–10 ft above floor, angled down to cover the door threshold and anyone entering or exiting.  
   •  Housing ideas: Integrate into a smoke-detector casing or ceiling-mount dome for a less obtrusive look.  
   •  Field of view (FOV): Choose a wide-angle (100°+) lens to catch facial detail without tilting.  

2. Living Room / Lounge  
   •  Ceiling-corner placement: One dome in the far corner captures the entire seating area and walkway.  
   •  Wall-mount above media console: Angles toward sofas, coffee-table zone, and corridor entrances.  
   •  Decorative concealment: Use a low-profile, flush-mount fixture that blends with existing light fixtures.  

3. Open-Plan Kitchen / Dining  
   •  Overhead beam or soffit: Positioned to watch island/counter edge and adjacent dining table.  
   •  Avoid direct view of personal storage (e.g. cabinets with guests’ belongings).  
   •  Ensure camera is splash-protected if above cooking areas.  

4. Hallway / Corridors  
   •  Mid-point ceiling mounts: One camera per long corridor to minimize blind spots.  
   •  Angle: Slightly downward so you see movement but not under door thresholds.  
   •  Lighting: Use cameras with good low-light or infrared capability for nighttime monitoring.  

5. Secondary Entry Points (Patio, Back Door, Balcony)  
   •  Exterior-rated bullet camera above the door, angled to capture steps or landing.  
   •  Mounted under eaves or overhangs to protect from weather and keep cable runs concealed.  
   •  Combine with motion-activated lighting to deter trespassers.  

6. Stairwells (if multi-level)  
   •  Ceiling dome at top of stairs: Monitors every floor transition.  
   •  Avoid pointing directly at neighbors’ doors if you share a hallway.  

General Best Practices  
 •  Mount at least 8 ft high—out of easy reach but with a clear view.  
 •  Balance FOV: wide enough to cover zones, narrow enough to capture identifying detail.  
 •  Keep cameras visible (or clearly disclosed in your listing) to deter wrongdoing.  
 •  Disable audio recording unless you’ve obtained clear guest consent.  
 •  Secure your video feeds with strong passwords and encrypted networks.  

By focusing on entry/exit points and high-traffic gathering spots—while avoiding private areas—you’ll enhance guest safety, deter theft, and maintain a welcoming environment.
